spec.title: PROP-074 — User project and per-project overrides: user-scoped packages, late boot lanes and user memory
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-08. Status `spec/plan`: the shape below is decided, the details are settled during implementation, which follows the cache-stable SYSTEM prefix work (campaign node `USER-PROJECT`, after `SYS-PROMPT`). Implementation evidence and owner acceptance are recorded separately: the bounded explicit workflow was accepted on 2026-11-17; this document is not a claim of full-feature completion. USER-PROJECT-CURRENT-SCOPE defines the current delivery boundary.

p.USER-PROJECT-PURPOSE: A user installs specification packages (flows, skills, stacks and the like) for themselves, not for one repository, with explicit `vibe install -g --user-project` as the recommended supported interface. Those packages form a separate tree in a per-user project. Every agent session in any vibevm project also loads that tree last, so it works as an advanced, structured, versioned `MEMORY.md` that follows the user across projects and machines.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT: One per-user project under the vibe settings root, a full ordinary vibevm project: its own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibevm/vibedeps/`, and an authored `vibevm/vibespecs/` tree (PROP/FEAT documents, boot sources, a user boot snippet). It is compiled, checked and updated by the same machinery as any project; no second compiler or loader exists.

p.USER-PROJECT-REUSE: The existing service user project that `vibe install -g mcp:…` materialises (PROP-027 REG-USER-PROJECT-MATERIALISATION) is the precedent. The specification project and the MCP service project remain separate under USER-PROJECT-ROOT-PATH and USER-PROJECT-ROOT-DECISION. A service scope is carried explicitly by the CLI, never inferred from a path.

p.USER-PROJECT-INSTALL: Explicit `vibe install -g --user-project`, `vibe update -g --user-project` and `vibe uninstall -g --user-project` target the personal specification project; `vibe list -g` and `vibe check -g` inspect it. Application and MCP packages keep their existing global destinations. These explicit personal operations reuse ordinary project laws (locked sources, rollback, cooperative stop). Automatic destination selection is convenience under USER-PROJECT-CURRENT-SCOPE, not a reason to weaken source integrity.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-PATH: The personal specification project lives at `<settings>/user-project`, where `<settings>` is resolved by the existing settings-root authority, including `VIBE_SETTINGS`. This is separate from the existing `<settings>/mcp/user-project` service project. No command migrates, merges or resets the MCP project implicitly. Runtime adapters resolve settings and pass the resulting root explicitly to ordinary project operations; a pure root calculation performs no filesystem or environment access.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT: `vibe user init` explicitly initializes the personal specification project without requiring a repository in the current directory. The initial manifest is an ordinary `[project]` manifest with `name = "vibe-user"` and `version = "1.0.0"`. It is not a package identity, service registration or globally unique user identifier. Authored records use the ordinary `vibevm/vibespecs/` layout. Initialization does not select a launcher, change harness settings, initialize Git, install packages, contact a registry, or create a SYSTEM template. Lockfiles and compiled boot outputs are produced only by their existing ordinary owners when needed, never fabricated by initialization.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-SAFETY: An absent root or an existing empty directory may be initialized. An existing valid ordinary project is preserved and reported as already initialized, without rewriting authored bytes or modification times. A nonempty directory without a valid project manifest, a malformed or unsupported manifest, a non-directory root, or a symbolic-link/reparse alias at the destination or an existing ancestor is an explicit refusal; initialization does not adopt, repair or overwrite it. Concurrent initializers must not overwrite each other's manifest. On failure or cancellation, preserve pre-existing user data and remove only operation-owned artifacts when their ownership is proven; otherwise report the incomplete state rather than deleting it speculatively.

p.USER-PROJECT-STATUS: `vibe user status` reports the resolved personal root and whether it is absent, initialized or unavailable, with the reason and explicit initialization or repair surface. An absent project is a normal status, not implicit permission to create it. An unavailable settings root or invalid existing project is reported as unavailable with a nonzero exit. Status performs no writes, installation, compilation, network access or harness launch. Boot and other read-only discovery paths likewise never initialize the project merely because it is absent.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-DECISION: Decision, 2026-11-15: keep the specification project separate and initialize it explicitly through ordinary project machinery. Why: the current MCP project owns service registrations and its own pinned dependency lifecycle; combining the roots would make personal specification operations alter service state without an explicit service scope. Rejected: silently reusing or migrating the MCP root, creating the personal project at every boot, and implementing a second manifest/lock/compiler stack. Revisit only when an owner-approved unified service/specification lifecycle defines registration, locking and migration semantics and its compatibility tests cover existing MCP installations. The root and initialization choices settle only this portion of USER-PROJECT-OPEN; routing, discovery, composition and override decisions remain separate work.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-ADMISSION: For these personal-root operations the selected settings path must be absolute. A relative value is reported as unavailable with a remedy naming an absolute `VIBE_SETTINGS`; it is not silently resolved against the invocation directory. Reject any parent-directory (`..`) component before filesystem access, even in an absolute path; do not normalize it across unverified ancestors. These selection/admission failures yield `root = null` and `outcome = refused` for both init and status, with no writes. The remedy names an absolute path without parent traversal; a syntactic refusal does not claim that a symlink was found. Before creating any ancestor or other output, validate every selected-root component against the existing safe-filesystem admission rules. A component that cannot be represented losslessly by that layer, including a non-UTF-8 normal component, is an unsupported-path refusal with root=null for either command; never replace bytes lossily or begin mutation before discovering that refusal. Name the representation limitation and recommend a supported absolute settings path, rather than claiming the path is absent or corrupt. This limitation follows the existing safe-filesystem component representation, not a second personal-project parser; revisit when that shared layer supports lossless native path components and its consumer tests cover them. This admission rule does not change the existing settings resolver or other commands' treatment of relative overrides. Reason: an ordinary change of working directory must not select another personal project. Revisit only with an explicit stable base for relative personal-root bindings; implicit cwd resolution is rejected.

p.USER-PROJECT-INITIALIZED-CRITERION: Initialized means that a bounded, stable, no-follow read of the root `vibe.toml` passes the ordinary in-memory manifest parser and semantic validation and contains `[project]`. A project that also declares `[workspace]` is admitted; a package-only or virtual-workspace-only manifest is not. This observation does not traverse workspace members, validate neighboring SYSTEM inputs, inspect lock integrity or establish boot freshness. Status identifies this limited scope rather than claiming the whole project is healthy. Existing projects need no authored directory to qualify, and init never fills missing directories in an already initialized project.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-PUBLICATION: For a newly initialized project, the persistent output set is `vibe.toml` plus empty `vibevm/` and `vibevm/vibespecs/` directories, along with any missing ancestors of the selected root. No other authored files, boot directory, lockfile or ignore file is created. Prepare the authored directories before publishing the manifest with no-replace semantics; the manifest is the initialization visibility boundary. Temporary operation-owned staging is allowed but is never mistaken for an initialized project. Do not create a project lock or other file before classifying an existing directory as admissible. Status on an absent root or an empty root without a manifest reports absent; nonempty residue without an admitted manifest reports unavailable.

p.USER-PROJECT-INIT-RACES: Concurrent init permits one creator and another observer returning already initialized after independently admitting the published manifest. A contender that observes pre-publication nonempty state or input movement may instead refuse with an explicit concurrent-or-incomplete-state diagnostic and retry guidance; success for every contender is not promised. Never interpret arbitrary residue as proof of another initializer's ownership. Failure before manifest publication may leave explicitly reported incomplete directories when safe cleanup cannot be proved. Cancellation after successful publication reports that initialization was committed rather than rolling back a project another process may already use. No command automatically repairs or deletes ambiguous residue.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT: Init and status share one typed observation, protocol `vibe-user-project/1`, registered as `cli-user-project-report` with authoritative schema `schemas/user_project_report.jtd.json`. Required fields are `protocol`, `ok` (boolean), `command` (`user:init` or `user:status`), `root` (nullable string), `state` (`absent`, `initialized`, `unavailable`), `outcome` (`created`, `already-initialized`, `observed`, `refused`, `incomplete`), `effects` (`none`, `changed`, `unknown`), `publication` (`not-started`, `restored`, `committed`, `recovery-required`), and nullable `reason` and `remedy` strings. Root is the admitted absolute path in the existing machine-path encoding, even if it does not exist; missing or relative settings yield null, never an empty string or cwd guess. No manifest content, credential, timestamp or user identity is included. Existing optional CLI context stamps remain transport metadata.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT-EFFECTS: Effects describe only this invocation, not old residue or another initializer: `none` means no surviving owned mutation is established and none is uncertain; `changed` means surviving owned changes are established; `unknown` means their survival cannot be determined. Publication refers to this invocation's initialization transaction, not merely to the existence of a manifest: `not-started` means no mutating initialization began, `restored` means its effects were proven undone, `committed` means manifest publication succeeded, and `recovery-required` means mutation began but neither completion nor full restoration is established. Created maps to initialized/created/changed/committed with ok=true. Reinit maps to initialized/already-initialized/none/not-started with ok=true. After root selection is admitted, status maps to observed/none/not-started, with ok=true for absent or initialized and false for unavailable. Failure to select or admit a root (including unavailable settings, a relative path or parent traversal) instead maps to unavailable/refused/none/not-started with root=null for either command. An init refusal before writes likewise maps to unavailable/refused/none/not-started; retain its root when selection itself was admitted. A failed mutating init maps to unavailable/incomplete with ok=false, effects and publication reported from actual evidence. Pre-existing incomplete residue alone never implies changed or recovery-required for a read-only observer. An unknown write outcome is not encoded as changed=true.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-REPORT-TRANSPORT: In JSON mode successful operations emit one root report on stdout through the existing CLI context renderer. Typed root-operation failures attach the same observation as the optional `user_project` member of the existing generic stderr error envelope, preserving its error chain and exit status; they do not first emit a root report on stdout. Errors before operation dispatch retain their existing envelope without a promised root observation. Acknowledged cancellation uses only the existing `vibe-project-cancellation/1` terminal envelope and exit 130, with the operation's publication state propagated accurately; it does not emit a second root terminal report. Existing progress events are not additional terminal reports. Plain and quiet output retain state, root when known, and actionable reason/remedy without pretending the observation is whole-project validation. The global JSON/context and cancellation contracts are not replaced by this feature.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT-GRAMMAR: The initial grammar is `vibe user init` and `vibe user status`, with existing global output and cancellation options inherited. Neither verb accepts a positional root, `--path`, `-g`, `--force` or a second root override; the existing settings authority is the sole selector. Later operations are not shipped as placeholder commands. Status is a read-only metadata operation; initialization uses the existing finite-operation progress convention.

p.USER-PROJECT-DESTINATION: The destination is distinct from package identity, declared kind and installed capability. Add `--user-project`, requiring `-g`, to install, update and uninstall as the explicit selector for the personal specification project. It is not a path override or a new package-reference prefix. Kind prefixes retain ordinary manifest-kind validation. Without this selector, preserve successful existing application, MCP and remap routes as defined below; do not turn a formerly successful application installation into a specification installation merely because its package also contains specifications. Non-global commands retain their existing behavior.

p.USER-PROJECT-INSTALL-ROUTING: For unqualified global install, literal `mcp:` references retain service installation and registration; valid remap packages retain their dedicated offer/consent owner. Other resolved packages with a valid application declaration retain application installation, including dual-form packages. Packages admitted by ordinary consumer-project dependency installation, without an application declaration and outside those dedicated routes, target the personal project. Explicit `-g --user-project` selects ordinary specification dependency installation even for a dual-form package, without running its application installer, registering MCP servers or applying remap offers. It does not bypass ordinary package admission: doc packages retain their cache/reader remedy and remap packages retain their dedicated owner, not personal dependencies. Explicit personal selection combined with a literal service-routing `mcp:` reference refuses as conflicting intent; no service installation is silently reinterpreted. Do not infer capability from a filename, a kind prefix alone or the mere presence of a specifications directory. Invalid manifests and failed resolution are errors, never evidence for choosing another destination.

p.USER-PROJECT-INSTALLED-ROUTING: Global update and uninstall of named packages choose from admitted installed state, not the newest registry manifest. Explicit `--user-project` consults only the personal manifest/lock and uses ordinary project reference matching. Without it, preserve literal MCP routes, the existing remap-uninstall priority and application ownership; a name that has no applicable installed legacy owner but identifies a personal requirement routes to the personal project. A coordinate installed in both stores retains its legacy default, and the diagnostic/help names `--user-project` to operate on the personal copy. This is explicit compatibility priority, not an invitation to mutate both stores. Failure or corruption of an applicable owner is reported, not treated as absence permitting fallback. Do not add a remap update implementation in this atom. Ordinary project aliases, versions and matching laws remain authoritative; do not create a second short-name resolver.

p.USER-PROJECT-EMPTY-AND-ALL: Explicit `install -g --user-project` without references installs the personal manifest requirements. Explicit `update -g --user-project` without references, or with `--all`, updates that project's requirements under ordinary update laws; named references narrow that owner normally. Unqualified `update -g --all` remains application-only, and unqualified empty global install/update retains its existing refusal rather than guessing a personal destination. Uninstall still requires one reference and gains no implicit all-stores operation. `list -g` and `check -g` select only the personal specification project; they are not an aggregate application/MCP/remap inventory. Their existing kind/output/check options retain meaning at the selected project. Non-global list/check remain unchanged.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROUTING-PREFLIGHT: One invocation has one destination. Resolve and validate the complete request's destination and incompatible flags before target-store or registration mutation; mixed-destination requests refuse with instructions to split commands. Existing destination-specific cardinality limits remain binding. Retain each acquired top-level manifest, exact version, source identity and verified content selection from routing preflight into execution; do not classify one mutable registry result and execute a second independently selected result. Use the ordinary resolver/materializer through an explicit selected-package handoff or immutable pinned source view, preserving transitive dependency resolution and integrity verification. Resolution may use ordinary source/cache machinery where allowed, but preview/no-write modes retain their existing stricter guarantees. No cross-store rollback transaction or new registry service is introduced. Full-tree continuation decision, 2026-11-17: the normal personal source factory remains authoritative for lock, declared policy and transitive resolution. It may readmit a routing root only by obtaining a genuine eligible candidate from its ordinary inventory with the same canonical binding, version, metadata recipe/digest and applicable content pin. Preserve original request site, kind and source constraints; equality alone grants no eligibility. Existing solver validation remains intact. The operation retains the original routing source and token for acquiring that admitted explicit root, validates the acquired payload against ordinary personal expected hashes/manifest, and uses the personal source owner for other dependencies. No forged tokens, post-solve source replacement or pointer-owner bypass is allowed. Preview retains private nonpublication storage through preflight and continuation. Startup observes stop input before persistent effects and performs cancellable classification before final destination-specific support admission; inferred personal stop is supported without silently enabling legacy app/MCP/remap cancellation. Install clarification, 2026-11-17: installed personal declarations do not override the application priority of unqualified global install; installed-state destination selection belongs to update/uninstall. If the final global selection is personal, it must also satisfy the personal project's ordinary declared/locked source policy. A conflicting source or version refuses before target mutation and names explicit --user-project as the way to resolve under that project's ordinary policy; never replace the routing candidate silently or ignore the lock. Different per-package source contexts do not by themselves constitute different destinations.

p.USER-PROJECT-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION: Personal lifecycle operations reuse the root selector and no-follow admission of section 2.1 and require an initialized ordinary project. An absent, invalid or unsafe personal project is an actionable failure naming `vibe user init` where appropriate, not permission to initialize, repair, fall back to the invocation directory or use the MCP root. An explicitly supplied `--path`, even `.`, conflicts with a personal destination; the parser's implicit default is not an explicit competing selector. Personal execution rejects application-installer and MCP-registration controls before writes rather than ignoring them. Ordinary dependency options, offline/source policy, rollback and cooperative cancellation are preserved. Keep applicability checks shared with the ordinary owners; the implementation brief requires a flag inventory before coding. List and check never install or initialize. Check reuses ordinary project health checks, not the deliberately limited root-status criterion.

p.USER-PROJECT-LIFECYCLE-TRANSPORT: Lifecycle commands retain their existing command-specific output formats, context stamps, error chains and cancellation protocol. `vibe-user-project/1` remains exclusively the root init/status observation, not a wrapper for install/list/check outputs. Personal selection is resolved before command execution and cancellation support classification; support cannot depend only on `global == false`. Preserve every legacy command's cancellation decision and do not acknowledge cancellation after a successful terminal document has already been emitted. Changes needed to any machine format require the existing schema/registry/codegen discipline, never hand-edited generated consumers or an undocumented extra JSON document.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROUTING-DECISION: Decision, 2026-11-15: compatibility-first destination selection with an explicit personal selector. Reason: package kind is not a capability selector, and existing dual-form application users must not silently switch stores. Rejected: routing every non-app kind to personal, making a kind prefix choose a store, updating all stores with existing `--all`, choosing by registry failure, and implicit initialization. Revisit only with an explicit compatibility/migration contract and tests for installed multi-store identities. This settles lifecycle routing only; late boot, override binding, memory and layered presentation remain separate work.

p.USER-LANE-SEPARATE: The user project produces its own boot lane from its own compilation. A repository's boot lane never embeds or copies it, so a teammate who clones the repository gets the identical project boot and no trace of another person's user lane.

p.USER-LANE-LAST: The user lane is always loaded dynamically, after the static lane, after every entry of the project's boot index and after any live continuation the SYSTEM work defines; only the project override lane (§5), when present, loads after it. A project may not reorder either earlier.

p.USER-LANE-OUTSIDE-PREFIX: The user lane never participates in the project's cache-stable SYSTEM prefix (`SYSTEM-PROMPT-SPEC`): changing or installing a user package never changes the project prefix bytes or invalidates its cache. It may enter only the separate, git-ignored composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX.

p.USER-LANE-ABSENT-OK: A missing, empty or broken user project never blocks a project session: the session boots as without it and diagnostics say what was skipped and why.

p.USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE: Loaded last does not mean ranked highest. Project rules (commit discipline, safety, attribution) bind whatever the user lane says; a user-lane statement that contradicts a project rule is reported, not obeyed. The exact precedence wording is part of the implementation.

memory.title: 4. User memory goes into the user project

p.USER-MEMORY-DEFAULT: By default, the facts an agent would otherwise write into a harness memory file (a local `MEMORY.md`, an auto-memory directory or similar) are written into the user project's `vibevm/vibespecs/` instead, as ordinary authored records that the user lane then loads.

p.USER-MEMORY-OPT-OUT: The default applies unless the user has explicitly decided otherwise and said so in a durable place (for example a setting in the user project or a statement in its user snippet). When opted out, agents use whatever memory mechanism the user chose and this law does not apply.

p.USER-MEMORY-CLASSIFICATION: The project-memory discipline still holds: a fact another contributor needs to build, review or understand a project belongs in that project's repository, never in the user project. Only facts about the user — preferences, working style, machine facts, cross-project conventions — go to the user project.

p.OVERRIDE-PURPOSE: Owner extension 2026-11-08. Everyone works with a project the same way, as recorded in git; a user who wants to work differently in that project keeps their own way in a per-user, per-project override project instead of committing it to the shared repository. The global user project supplies general personal preferences. The project override supplies the more specific personal choice. Precedence and delivery order are project, then global user project, then project override, subject to protected project rules; OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE is authoritative.

p.OVERRIDE-SHAPE: An override project is an ordinary vibevm project like the user project (§2): own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibedeps` and authored `vibevm/vibespecs`, its own compilation and its own boot lane. It never writes the project's tracked files or its lock, and a teammate's clone is unaffected by it.

p.OVERRIDE-LOCATION: Stored outside the checkout under the existing settings authority. Implementation decision, 2026-11-17: a stable user-chosen alias identifies an opaque local id and an ordinary project at <settings>/project-overrides/<opaque-id>. This is not the steward's exact checkout/revision tuple. For Git projects, lookup uses the canonical Git common directory plus the selected project node's workspace-relative path; branches do not change the binding, linked worktrees of the same repository/node share it, and different member nodes remain distinct. For non-Git projects, lookup uses the canonical project root. A new clone or moved non-Git project is unbound until the user explicitly binds it to the existing alias: override data and id survive, but no remote URL, project-name or content matching infers identity. A user-local mapping stores only alias, opaque id, necessary local locators and enabled state; no binding or personal path is written to shared project files. No credentials or remote identities are collected.

p.OVERRIDE-CONTROLS: Implementation decision, 2026-11-17: vibe user override init --alias NAME --path PROJECT explicitly creates and binds an ordinary override project; an exact repeat is idempotent, while alias reuse for a different identity or another alias already owning that identity refuses without adoption or overwrite. vibe user override bind --alias NAME --path PROJECT explicitly attaches a new checkout identity to an existing alias; conflicting ownership refuses. Init creates an enabled binding; bind preserves its enabled state. Status, enable and disable select the binding by --path PROJECT, defaulting to the invocation project when omitted; this path selects the shared project, never the settings root. Status is read-only and reports the override root for ordinary package operations through --path. Enable requires an existing valid binding/project; disable preserves all authored files and affects the next boot/launch, not instructions already loaded in a session. A missing or invalid mapping is diagnosed, not inferred, initialized or repaired by boot. Existing project initialization, safe filesystem and atomic local-metadata publication machinery own writes; failure reports incomplete state honestly, without introducing a new transaction/journal framework. Override packages use ordinary install/update/uninstall with the reported override root as --path.

p.OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE: Owner decision 2026-11-08: on conflict the more specific layer wins — project < global user project < project override. A per-project choice beats the user's general preference, as git's local beats global. Lanes load in the same order, project first, then the global user lane, then the project override lane, so the most specific text comes last. Non-overridable project rules still bind every layer (OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE).

p.OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE: Overrides add freely: extra packages, flows, skills, preferences. Taking away or replacing project rules is allowed only for what the project marks as overridable; commit discipline, attribution, safety and anything unmarked can only be supplemented. A layer statement contradicting a non-overridable project rule is reported, never obeyed (extends USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE).

p.OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION: Each layer has its own lock and is resolved and compiled separately in this task; a package an override needs at a version different from the project's lives in the override's own tree. The override lane loads dynamically, like the user lane (USER-LANE-LAST), and never enters the project's own cache-stable prefix; the composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX is the one place where the layers join.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX: In scope of this task (owner decision 2026-11-08): one cache-stable boot prefix composed from project + global user project + project override, in the precedence order of OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE, with resolution across the layers. The project layer, as the most shared and most stable bytes, comes first, so the project's own prefix stays a byte-identical leading part of the composed one. Without a user project or override the composed prefix equals the project prefix. Until a user composes layers, the separately loaded lanes of §3 and OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION remain the behaviour.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION: The composed prefix is personal and must never be committed. It is written inside the project's own `vibevm/` tree, next to the project's boot files, so an agent that looks around the file it was given finds the neighbouring files of the actual project and not of some other directory. The directory is ignored by a `.gitignore` that vibe writes into that directory itself (ignoring everything in it, including itself), never by editing the repository's root `.gitignore`. `vibe check` may issue a non-blocking warning when Git tracks the composed prefix or its directory; it does not prevent a deliberate user commit. Manual source/history publication remains the user's responsibility under USER-PROJECT-PRIVACY-RESPONSIBILITY. The reserved path is the selected project node's `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/local/`. Launch-only AGENT carriers and full composed SYSTEM artifacts are separate content-addressed files there.

p.OVERRIDE-NO-AI-NATIVE-ANCHORS: Owner decision 2026-11-08: shared project code never anchors to a local layer. Checks written in the AI-native languages (`spec://` references, `specmark` scopes and `#[spec]`-style annotations, coverage and status checks) may target only the project's own specifications and its declared dependencies — never the global user project or a project override. Otherwise code committed for everyone would cite specifications that a teammate's checkout does not have. The AI-native checkers refuse such a reference with a message naming the reference, the local layer it points into and the fix; a layer's own specifications are never counted toward the project's coverage or status. This needs an update of the AI-native packages (`org.vibevm.ai-native.core-ai-native`, the Rust and TypeScript language packages and their MCP servers) as part of this task.

p.AI-NATIVE-DECLARED-AUTHORITY: Full-tree authority decision, 2026-11-17: a Vibe project's shared code may target its own configured namespace and explicit external namespace aliases bound to exact admitted declared dependency specification roots for the selected node. Namespace aliases need not equal package coordinates; canonical owner root plus selected version/source binds an alias. A specmap external_specs row alone does not grant dependency authority to a Vibe project. Preserve the neutral engine dependency graph: use an explicit typed authority context from ordinary dependency owners/adapters, not a reverse dependency on host crates or another solver. All normalized scanner edges and Rust/TypeScript CLI/MCP check/write consumers enforce the same admitted namespace/root relation. Unknown, private or undeclared authorities refuse with offending reference and remedy, not only a dangling-edge warning; forbidden units cannot inflate coverage/status. Ambiguous or overlapping configured namespaces (a and a/b at the slash boundary) refuse with a distinct-alias remedy, not shadow or first-segment heuristics. Parse addresses with the existing grammar and match the complete unambiguous configured namespace. A Vibe project's authored self namespace may differ from its package coordinate: the host context records that exact namespace from the existing specmap configuration and fingerprints its presence/bytes, while preserving self coordinate as separate owner identity. Standalone consumers require exact context/config namespace agreement; changing config invalidates context. Generic projects retain their established namespace convention under the same non-overlap rule. Ordinary missing-anchor diagnostics remain separate. Personal/override projects may analyze their own units independently, never siblings implicitly.

p.AI-NATIVE-GENERIC-COMPATIBILITY: Generic AI-native projects without a Vibe manifest retain their existing explicitly configured external_specs authority; they need not adopt Vibe manifests. Private-layer exclusion and safe root admission still apply. An existing malformed, unsafe or unsupported Vibe manifest is an error, never grounds to downgrade to generic authority. Canonical load/entrypoints must not silently omit required Vibe authority context; standalone consumers require an ordinary bridge or an explicit actionable refusal, not a fallback that trusts arbitrary external roots. Deriving any necessary manifest/lock view must use existing canonical generated formats or one ordinary adapter with parity tests, not copied manifest parsers or a new resolution service. No ambient HOME inventory, secret search or model-based reference classifier is introduced.

p.AI-NATIVE-AUTHORITY-BRIDGE: The ordinary host workspace/install compilation owner produces a registered typed derived .vibe/specmap-authority.json artifact per analyzed selected node. It records selected project identity, admitted dependency coordinates/versions/specification roots and necessary exact manifest/lock/dependency-manifest input fingerprints, without timestamps, credentials or authored contents. Root authority is projected from the ordinary planner's accepted per-consumer root edges and finalized selected-node inputs, including actual configured, conditional and weak selections; a workspace-wide lock union or raw manifest traversal cannot grant selected-node authority. Carry that narrow projection through existing plan/apply outcomes into the publisher and reuse it with actual durable dependency edges for relation admission. Ready/no-op paths must retain or obtain the ordinary locked metadata projection without a second independently invented resolver or acquisition. Presence/absence fingerprints cover source/configuration inputs that shape this projection. Namespace aliases remain configured specmap rows and must map to these admitted roots. Standalone canonical engines consume the generated format and validate bounded no-follow input fingerprints and selected-root identity before scanning external specifications; they do not duplicate the host manifest parser or dependency solver. Any existing Vibe manifest selects this regime; missing/stale authority context is an actionable ordinary install/regeneration refusal, never generic fallback. An ordinary vibe install --path ROOT generates context even for a no-dependency personal project; root init output is unchanged, check/status/read paths never generate or migrate context. Successful update, uninstall and reinstall refresh authority from their own final admitted operation world before reporting complete, preserving existing offline/no-resolve contracts where those operations require them. Use the operation's exact per-node roots and durable edges, not a new registry lookup or arbitrary pruning of an old context. A post-publication refresh failure reports the actual committed lifecycle effects and actionable regeneration remedy; it does not falsely claim rollback or silently reuse stale authority. Unchanged multi-node authority publication is canonical and preserves bytes/mtime. Generic non-Vibe projects retain their existing explicit configuration authority. The derived artifact is freshness/provenance metadata under the ordinary same-user trust model, not a signature or defense against deliberate simultaneous rewriting of sources and derived data.

p.LAYERS-IN-TREE: Owner request 2026-11-08: `vibe tree` (plain, console TUI and vibeterm views, PROP-036) shows all three layers correctly — which layer each package, document and boot lane comes from, the effective result after precedence, and what a more specific layer supplements or replaces — and lets the user switch override layers on and off: hiding a layer in the view, and enabling or disabling a layer for the project itself (which then drops out of loading and of the composed prefix). The plain and JSON forms carry the same layer attribution. Implementation decision, 2026-11-17: preserve the frozen existing tree --json v1 document; tree --layers --json opts into a separately registered layered-tree envelope containing the unchanged project tree and ordered project/user/override descriptors with enabled state, availability, diagnostics and ordinary per-layer tree payloads when available. Identity is layer-qualified; equal package coordinates across stores are not merged. Disabled and unavailable layers remain visible as descriptors. View hide/show is not persisted loading state and does not silently remove layers from the default JSON census. Initial effective participation means enabled and available additive content, not an inferred replacement relation. Plain --layers and later console/vibeterm controls consume the same read model; unsupported enable controls are explicit, not invented as view toggles.

p.LAYER-USER-CONTROLS: Full-tree completion includes per-project enable/disable of the global user layer independently from project override. vibe user enable or disable --path PROJECT controls the next load in that selected project; absence defaults enabled. This is user-local state keyed by the same admitted project identity, not a mutation of shared project files or the global user project. Creating this control must not initialize an override project or require an alias. Use the existing override-binding mapping file, lock and safe publication owner, with a distinct user_controls array of identity plus user_enabled, not Binding.enabled or an alias. Writers publish mapping schema2; readers admit schema1 with empty controls/default enabled and strict schema2. Only an explicit mutation upgrades schema1; status/boot reads never migrate or create metadata. Old schema1 binaries may explicitly refuse schema2; forward-read compatibility is not claimed. Duplicate or conflicting control identities refuse. No new settings file or storage framework is introduced. Classic discovery, capture, launch, compose and tree consume the same observed selection. Tree view hide/show never changes this setting; explicit user/override loading controls persist separately. The mandatory project layer cannot be disabled. Unavailable control metadata is diagnosed without fabricating a successful selection or blocking the mandatory project boot.

p.LAYER-EXPLICIT-RELATIONS: Owner completion mandate, 2026-11-17: implement the remaining explicit relations, authority and automatic routing requirements; the earlier bounded release is not the final scope. Canonical ordinary manifest metadata has optional [layers] with schema=1, absent preserving existing behavior. Each [[layers.targets]] declares a node-local stable id, source as an ordinary own/dependency spec URI with an explicit anchor, policy protected (default) or overridable, and category preference (default), safety, attribution or commit-discipline. The last three categories cannot be overridable. A source resolves to exactly one admitted anchor-addressed specification unit; document root anchors are allowed, package-wide removal is not. The owning lower layer alone grants overridability. Upper [[layers.relations]] declares id, kind supplement or replace, target_layer project or user, target as the lower declared target id, and source as an admitted anchor URI in the upper layer's ordinary own/dependency scope. Same-layer or upward targets refuse; namespace/path guessing never grants authority. Installed packages may contribute declarations only from the analyzed node's admitted dependency closure at its locked version/source. Preserve the declaring coordinate as provenance; target identity is lower layer plus declaring owner plus id, not a flattened id. An optional target_owner package coordinate selects that lower admitted package; absence selects the lower layer's root declaration. A package's own declaration defaults to its own owner, never impersonates the root. Package declarations cannot grant replacement authority over a different owner's source: an overridable grant must address that declaring owner's own unit. Root declarations may expose dependency units as protected targets or supplement them, but cannot relabel a dependency's protected unit as overridable. Source URIs remain version-bound by the same ordinary selected world; no extra source_owner field or registry lookup is introduced.

p.LAYER-EFFECTIVE-RELATIONS: A supplement adds a declared relation without replacing the lower unit. Replace requires a lower overridable preference target; protected, absent, ambiguous and unsafe targets refuse with source, target, layer and remedy. Competing replacement sources in one layer for the same target refuse. Project override may supersede a user's replacement of the same original project target when that original target permits replacement; the highest enabled, available and validated layer wins, and intermediate relations are shown as superseded. Disabled or unavailable relations are inactive and leave lower content effective. Effective precedence is finalized against layers actually admitted for that request and its session-target conditions, not merely an earlier compiled-graph observation. A later optional-layer load failure or unresolved target cannot leave a successfully delivered lower replacement marked superseded by content that was skipped. Reuse one admitted selection/result for relation notices and delivery; tree distinguishes declaration availability from request-effective participation where a target observation is required. No prose contradiction detection or NLP authority is inferred. Invalid relations skip the offending optional layer with a diagnostic, preserving project and independently valid other layers. Source authorization and anchor existence are checked through ordinary parsers/manifest/dependency owners.

p.LAYER-RELATION-TRANSPORT: One workspace-owned validated relation result drives tree, capture, launch and compose. Preserve exact shared project leading bytes: do not physically remove target text from the project prefix or rewrite its authored files. Deliver an explicit authorized relation notice after complete project continuation and before the affected upper-layer material, naming exact target/source and effective precedence. It states supersession of the declared overridable unit, never blanket cancellation of project rules. Layered tree reports active, superseded, disabled, unavailable or denied relations, layer-qualified identities and reasons; plain, JSON, console and hosted views agree. Evolve the opt-in layered envelope to schema epoch2 with documented compatibility and registered schema/consumer updates; legacy project tree v1 remains unchanged. Independent layer locks and compilation remain independent; cross-layer relation resolution is not dependency-lock merging.

p.USER-PROJECT-PRIVACY-RESPONSIBILITY: Owner refinement, 2026-11-17: distinguish product-created leakage from deliberate user publication. Shared project boot and its cache-stable prefix never contain personal-layer bytes or machine-specific personal bindings. Personal composed artifacts live only in the selected node's boot/local directory, with an in-directory .gitignore ignoring everything including itself; external user projects are not exporter traversal inputs. Ordinary filesystem-copy publication excludes that reserved subtree before descent. Credentials are not boot or memory content. Document that ignores do not protect already tracked files or override git add -f, and that users must not commit or publish personal/composed boot artifacts. Preventing deliberate commits, scanning secrets, rejecting or sanitizing all tracked trees and historical Git objects, and policing explicitly requested faithful Git history export are not USER-PROJECT requirements. Those routes retain ordinary identity and publication laws: never silently strip content while claiming the original tree/history identity. A cheap tracked-path warning may assist the user but is non-blocking and must not read private contents. Existing unrelated confidentiality rules are not weakened.

p.USER-PROJECT-DELIVERY-BOUNDARY: Owner refinement, 2026-11-17: deliver user-visible vertical increments using ordinary project machinery. First integrate and demonstrate explicit user init/status with a freshly source-bound CLI and isolated settings, independently of later native/retained transaction work. Next connect personal package lifecycle and an actual late-boot transport. Judge each increment by runnable command/output and adjacent compatibility, not counts of cleared internal prerequisites. A separate retained filesystem/native framework, general Windows private allocation, universal hostile-writer exclusion and complete history privacy policing are removed from USER-PROJECT scope, not deferred work. Preserve concrete source-integrity, no-overwrite/data-loss, secret-isolation, destination and honest cancellation/publication guarantees. Delete the campaign-only implementation and active instructions for those unnecessary mechanisms; do not preserve them as optional follow-up inputs, archives or backlog. Preserve unrelated existing product machinery and the useful root init/status implementation. Incremental delivery does not delete remaining override/memory/AI-native/tree obligations or silently disable supported modes; any limitation is explicit and does not count as whole-feature acceptance.

p.USER-PROJECT-CURRENT-SCOPE: Owner refinement, 2026-11-17: the accepted practical workflow uses explicit --user-project for personal mutations and ordinary --path for override package operations. Complete user scenarios take priority over perfecting convenience routing. The earlier bounded milestone allowed automatic existing-context and inferred-cancellation refusals. The owner's subsequent full-tree mandate supersedes those completion exemptions: implement ordinary personal source-policy continuation and cancellable classification as specified in USER-PROJECT-ROUTING-PREFLIGHT, preserving explicit commands and legacy compatibility. Actual conflicting source selections still refuse before mutation; an existing nonempty context alone is no longer a final unsupported-mode excuse. Do not ignore locks, mutate during preview or replace ordinary owners with a new source-authority subsystem. Existing successful app/MCP/remap routes remain compatibility obligations; concrete defects in their supported behavior require focused disposition.

p.USER-PROJECT-MEMORY-DELIVERY: Memory delivery is authorized authored records with ordinary INDEX enrollment or an explicit link from an authored boot snippet, followed by next-request loading. Durable user-snippet opt-out selects the chosen alternative without a preference parser. Boot/read paths do not write or initialize. An authorized first-write request without an available personal project receives an explicit initialization/remedy; no silent harness-memory fallback. Autonomous model fact extraction, automatic harness-memory migration and cross-machine synchronization are not implementation prerequisites for this delivery. They are not demonstrated by an authored-record test.

p.USER-PROJECT-TRANSPORT-DELIVERY: Classic entrypoints carry machine-independent late reading instructions without requiring a SYSTEM template; launch composes a private carrier through existing harness adapters; capture reports the prepared layered request; explicit vibe prompt compose publishes a private full-prefix artifact whose leading project bytes are unchanged. Project live continuation precedes personal layers. No product session API sender presently consumes that artifact: do not inject personal boot into installer or package-step agent requests or invent an API sender to claim coverage. Reading contracts, hermetic argv/PTY delivery and disk artifact consumption are distinguished from actual model compliance, graphical smoke and provider consumption.

p.USER-PROJECT-CLOSURE-ACCOUNTING: Root selection, routing policy, override identity and controls, composed artifact location, memory enrollment/opt-out and layered wire format are settled by this record. Remaining implementation or validation gaps are not unresolved architecture by default. The final builder outcome must classify every original obligation as demonstrated, concrete supported-scenario defect, explicit unsupported convenience, unrun validation or owner-excluded scope. In particular, additive layer attribution is not a replacement graph, bounded private-root exclusion is not universal dependency authority, and independent layer compilation does not merge cross-layer package locks. Never mark those broader requirements implemented without evidence. The current completion brief is campaigns/user-project-2026-11/briefs/UP-COMPLETE-01.md; it supersedes the earlier bounded UP-FINISH-01 scope after the owner explicitly requested the three remaining tasks and the USER-PROJECT tree; it authorizes routine scoped local fixation and implementation continuation under the owner's final instruction, not external push or release. Final feature acceptance remains the owner's, separate from architecture/task closure.
